title: Inside the Rise of Autonomous AI Hackers: XBOW's Oege de Moor
summary: XBOW's founder pitches autonomous AI hacking, citing a Bing RCE and a HackerOne leaderboard win, and warns that defenders must adopt AI quickly.

assertions.quote: This vulnerability was found by the product of my company, Xbo. And the only input it needed was the URL.

verdicts.note: By 2025-26 AI systems (Big Sleep, AIxCC entrants, lab red-team reports) found many confirmed real vulnerabilities, though false positives remain common and human triage is still needed.

assertions.quote: Within a few weeks, Xbo first became the number one hacker in the United States

verdicts.note: XBOW did top HackerOne's US leaderboard, but that ranking rewards volume and many findings were lower severity, so it doesn't show parity with the best humans.

assertions.quote: For most CVEs, it is already being exploited before the the CVE is even published.

verdicts.note: Mandiant and others report time-to-exploit falling to days and many zero-days exploited before disclosure, but 'most CVEs' overstates it and AI's role is unproven.

assertions.quote: This is much better than either model separately.

verdicts.note: Plausible because model errors are partly uncorrelated, but the evidence is the vendor's own benchmark with no independent replication.
